newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy budget fringe benefits tax focuses on cars.
newsitem.headline: Italy budget fringe benefits tax focuses on cars.

text.p: Italy's 1997 financial budget tax on fringe benefits will focus on company cars in its aim of raising 2.56 trillion lire of extra revenue, Italian newspapers reported on Sunday.
The tax on comany cars is aimed at raising 2.47 trillion lire, while the other revenue will come from higher taxes on luncheon vouchers, on easy-term loans and on payments in kind.
The extra revenue from company cars is based on an average number of 290,000 company cars in use in Italy, and the higher taxes will be related to the useage of company cars.

The complete 1997 financial package will cut 62.5 trillion lire off Italy's deficit. The basic budget will cut 37.5 trillion lire off the deficit with 25 trillion lire coming from planned spending cuts and 12.5 trillion from new revenue.
In addition, 13 trillion lire will be raised from a special Euro Tax and 12 trillion lire from unspecified "Treasury operations."
